summary: Spill, a Twitter/X competitor founded by laid-off Twitter employee Alphonzo Terrell, marked its one-year anniversary at AfroTech in Austin with a $2 million extension led by Collide Capital, bringing pre-seed funding to $5 million. The invite-only beta app, aimed at Black Americans and the LGBTQ community, has about 200,000 users and launched a Live-like feature called Tea Party, first hosted by Kerry Washington. The article contrasts Spill's community-first approach with other Twitter alternatives and the shutdown of Pebble, and notes plans to exit beta and pay creators.
one_line: Spill, a community-focused Twitter alternative founded by a laid-off Twitter employee, raised a $2M extension, hit 200,000 users, and launched Tea Party at AfroTech.
key_facts: Alphonzo Terrell toasted the one-year anniversary of being laid off from Twitter with Dom Pérignon at an AfroTech after-party in Austin.
Spill has about 200,000 users and is still in beta; it positions itself as a safer place for Black Americans and the LGBTQ community.
Spill has raised a total of $5 million in pre-seed funding, including a $2 million extension round led by Collide Capital (a correction noted it is $2 million, not $2.75 million).
Spill launched an invite-only beta in June and went viral within three weeks.
Terrell was laid off from Twitter amid Elon Musk's acquisition, along with about 3,000 others, then spent three days in an Airbnb making the pitch deck with former colleague DeVaris Brown.
Kapor Capital wrote Spill's first check after TechCrunch covered the founding; over 25,000 people joined the waitlist in less than 24 hours from that article.
Threads got 100 million sign-ups within five days, Mastodon has 1.8 million monthly active users, and Bluesky hit 1 million users in September.
Pebble (formerly T2), led by CEO Gabor Cselle, shut down after a year with just 20,000 registered users.
At AfroTech, Terrell interviewed Mitch and Freida Kapor and unveiled Tea Party, a feature similar to Instagram Live; Kerry Washington was the first host.
Spill has 'not paid for a single acquisition to date,' according to Kenya Parham, Global VP of Community and Partnerships.
Terrell previously led marketing teams at HBO and Showtime; advertising partners include Netflix, Lionsgate, VH1, Showtime and Sony Pictures.
Spill is set to exit beta and open to the public next year, and plans to pay creators for their cultural contributions.
